title: Review of c07 ringswim c2 (SIBM, L4b[L3]): crescents swim on fresh seed 7, but the link ring is below threshold (1.32) and the population fuses into one band by t~9600; Weak
summary: Re-ran world_claim.py on seed 7 (200 frames x 100 steps) and world_chi0.py on the same seed. From noise, walled cells form by t=800 and swim as crescents with a depletion wake through t~7900 (rerun/seed7/sheet.png), but from t~6900 they line up and fuse into a single domain-wrapping band that persists to t=20000 (final 2 components), the failure the author reports only for waste=0 on seed 1. The L ring is rim/core 1.32 (7/19 cells membrane-like) against 1.11 with chi=0 (0/139), so the chi operator does make a ring but it is below the 1.5 gate on this seed, as on the author's seed 1 (1.27).

observations.M: rerun/seed7/sheet.png t=1700-7900: crescents with a trailing depletion wake move several body lengths with the body plan kept

seeds_run.result: partial: swimming ringed cells until t~8000, then fusion into one band; L rim/core 1.32 < 1.5

controls_run.B: chi0/seed7 (chi=0, same seed): L rim/core 1.11, 0/139 membrane-like

verdicts.limitation: B fails the 1.5 gate on seed 7 (1.32) as on the author's seed 1 (1.27), so the ring holds on 2 of 4 seeds; after t~9600 there are no individuals on seed 7, so labkit's 21.7 body-length maximum includes the band and is not a cell displacement; I did not rerun mu=0.
